text: Here is your homework this week. Every morning before you check your phone, read one psalm. Just one. Monday, Psalm 1. Tuesday, Psalm 2. By Friday you will have read five psalms and you will notice something. The psalms teach you how to talk to God. They give you words when you do not have any. Blessed is the man who walks not in the counsel of the wicked. He is like a tree planted by streams of water that yields its fruit in its season. Notice the tree does not try to produce fruit. It just stays planted. Fruit comes in its season. Some of you are frustrated because you do not see fruit yet. Stay planted. The wicked are like chaff that the wind drives away. Chaff is light. It has no roots. It goes wherever the wind goes. The question is not how strong you feel today. The question is what you are rooted in. Jesus said, abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit by itself unless it abides in the vine, neither can you unless you abide in me. That is the whole Christian life in one word. Abide.

text: I did a funeral last month for a man I had never met. His family did not go to church. The funeral home called and asked if I would do it. And I sat with that family in a little room and they told me about him. He fixed lawnmowers for every widow on his street and never charged them. He coached Little League for twenty years. Nobody in that room knew if he believed in God. And I had to stand up and say something true. Here is what I said. I said, I do not know this man's heart, but I know the heart of God. And the heart of God is revealed at the cross. Paul says in First Thessalonians 4 that we do not grieve as those who have no hope. He does not say we do not grieve. Christians grieve. Jesus wept at the tomb. But we grieve with hope because death is not the last word. For since we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so, through Jesus, God will bring with him those who have fallen asleep. Fallen asleep. That is how the New Testament talks about the death of a believer. You do not fear sleep. You expect to wake up.

text: When I was a kid our church bulletin had a typo that I still remember. It said the potluck would be followed by a prayer and medication. That is funny but it also tells you something about how we think of prayer. We think of it like medicine. Take it when you feel bad. But Paul says pray without ceasing. That is not medicine. That is breathing. You do not breathe only when you feel sick. Prayer is the native air of the soul. Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances, for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you. People ask me all the time what is God's will for my life. Here it is, in black and white. Rejoice. Pray. Give thanks. Start there, and the rest gets clearer. Do not quench the Spirit. Do not despise prophecies, but test everything, hold fast what is good.
